summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: ABO is controlled by I gene (IA, IB, i). Group O is universal donor; Group AB is universal recipient. Erythroblastosis fetalis occurs when an Rh- mother carries a second Rh+ fetus (prevented by RhoGAM anti-D IgG).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 2.1 The ABO Blood Group System (Karl Landsteiner, 1900)
Determined by the presence or absence of two surface carbohydrate antigens (**Antigen A** and **Antigen B**) on the RBC membrane, controlled by the $I$ gene ($\text{ABO}$ locus on chromosome 9) with three alleles ($I^A, I^B, i$). $I^A$ and $I^B$ show codominance ($I^A I^B \rightarrow \text{Group AB}$).

### 2.2 The Rh System & Erythroblastosis Fetalis
The **Rh Antigen (D Antigen)** is an inherited protein present on the RBC membrane of $\approx 80\%$ of humans ($\text{Rh}^+$ positive). Individuals lacking this antigen are $\text{Rh}^-$ negative.

```
                      ERYTHROBLASTOSIS FETALIS CASCADE
                      
   Mother ($\text{Rh}^-$) carrying First $\text{Rh}^+$ Fetus ──► Fetal $\text{Rh}^+$ blood leaks into mother during delivery
                                                                     │
   Mother produces anti-$\text{Rh}$ IgG antibodies ◄─────────────────────────┘
                                     │
   Second $\text{Rh}^+$ Pregnancy ──► Maternal anti-$\text{Rh}$ IgG crosses placenta into fetal circulation
                                     │
   Fetal RBC Hemolysis ──► Severe Anemia, Jaundice, & Kernicterus (**Erythroblastosis Fetalis**)
```

* **Clinical Prevention**: Administering anti-$\text{Rh}$ antibodies (**RhoGAM / Anti-D Immunoglobulin**) to the $\text{Rh}^-$ mother immediately after the delivery of the first $\text{Rh}^+$ child neutralizes fetal $\text{Rh}^+$ RBCs before maternal sensitization occurs.
